parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police targeting, no universal-exposure rule (no facility, custody, or border mandate), and no documented incidents against trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal, so the sexuality statute is not a lever here. Offsetting: the dossier's worst features are tier 3-5 — general LGBTQ stigmatisation (not trans-broken-down), a lukewarm, dated 2016 LGBTQ poll, and protections/hate-crime grounds that name only sexual orientation, so nothing names gender identity. Document-mismatch handling at borders is an open question, not a documented exposure. Data is thin (encyclopedic, unmonitored), so silence is not safety, but structural signals — decriminalisation, no recognition regime reaching visitors, no organised hostility — point away from severe tiers. No documented acceptance or working remedy holds it below the acceptance-with-protections tier.
